citation: Kinzie, Juliette A. M. Wau-Bun: The 'Early Day' in the North-West. New York: Derby & Jackson, 1856.
author: Juliette Augusta Magill Kinzie
note: The only near-contemporary descriptive text for the Wolf Point buildings. Load-bearing for the Sauganash: 'a pretentious white two-story building, with bright-blue wooden shutters, the admiration of all the little circle at Wolf Point.' Written 25 years after the events and describing 1831, not 1835 — hence tier 2 and the describes_date field. Also the source for the Indian Agency house ('logs hewed and squared, with a centre, two wings') and for the Wolf Point name deriving from an Indian resident called Moa-way, 'the Wolf'.
access_notes: The authorama.com transcription used during research has no Wayback snapshot; archived_url therefore points at a scanned edition of the book itself (1901 printing of the 1856 text), which is the durable citable copy. Verify chapter XVII page numbers against that scan before quoting a page.
